newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Rocca to head local bank Banco Finasa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Rocca to head local bank Banco Finasa.

text.p: Brazilian private bank Banco Mercantil de Sao Paulo said Carlos Antonio Rocca, the board president of retailer Casa Anglo, will head its investment bank Banco Finasa de Investimentos.
Rocca, who headed Casa Anglo's board of directors for 15 years, is due to start working for Finasa early May, said Raul Pereira Barreto, senior vice-president at Mercantil de Sao Paulo.
Barreto said Rocca's entry in Finasa is part of the bank's strategy to strengthen its capital markets and mergers and acquisitions businesses.
"We are betting on investment banking. With the economic stability, there is room to invest and expand in this business," he said.
Rocca will replace Gastao Augusto de Bueno Vidigal, president of Mercantil de Sao Paulo's administrative council, who was also heading Finasa, Barreto said.
Rocca said he has agreed with Casa Anglo, the holding company for Mappin department store, to remain in his post until April 30, when the firm's shareholders meet.

Banco Mercantil de Sao Paulo is a commercial bank, with 199 branches. Last week, the bank showed a net profit of 161.5 million reais, with a 9.64 percent return on equity, according to Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper.
